page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-240GB-1xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor with 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.0 GB of RAM per core. Crucially, it integrates a single NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU with 192 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included on this instance type, and it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data highlights the server's capabilities, particularly in memory bandwidth and specialized processing. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in LLM inference speed using a small 135M model, delivering 9953.26 tokens per second for prompt processing and 525.92 tokens per second for text generation. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance, reaching 4156.98 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 251.17 GB/sec for large-block reads. CPU performance is supported by advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contributed to a strong Passmark CPU score of 52754.5 and an extended instructions score of 67506.68.

A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation model and the absence of local storage, meaning storage must be attached externally. However, the high density of system memory combined with the 192 GB of Blackwell GPU VRAM offers high resource density for memory-intensive operations. This hardware profile is highly efficient for workloads that offload heavy computation to the GPU. The server is optimized for large language model inference, deep learning, data science pipelines, and high-throughput database operations.
